title: Intermittent disconnections on fibre broadband during peak hours
body:
Use this procedure when a customer reports repeated drops at the same time of day on an otherwise working fibre line.

Procedure:
1. Check the ONT/fibre terminal for a red LOS light and note the optical power level in the line diagnostics.
2. Run a 24-hour line stability test from the provisioning portal to look for evening packet loss and re-syncs.
3. Check for congestion on the customer's GPON port and node during 19:00-23:00.
4. Move the customer to a less loaded port or raise a network capacity ticket if utilisation is above 85%.
5. Replace the patch cable and re-seat the fibre connector if optical power is outside -8 to -27 dBm.
6. Call back after 48 hours to confirm the drops have stopped.

Escalation: if the problem persists after the steps above, raise a Tier-2 ticket referencing bb_evening_drops and attach the diagnostics collected.

title: Fiber speeds lower than the subscribed plan
body:
Follow these checks when measured throughput is consistently below the plan speed.

Procedure:
1. Run a wired speed test directly from the ONT-connected laptop to separate Wi-Fi issues from line issues.
2. Verify the provisioned profile matches the plan in billing and correct any speed-profile mismatch.
3. Check line statistics for errors, CRC counts and optical power on the ONT.
4. Ask the customer to disconnect bandwidth-heavy devices and retest to rule out local saturation.
5. Reprovision the profile and reboot the ONT remotely, then retest wired speeds.
6. Escalate to the access-network team if wired speeds stay under 70% of the plan.

Escalation: if the problem persists after the steps above, raise a Tier-2 ticket referencing bb_slow_speed and attach the diagnostics collected.

title: Total loss of fibre broadband service (LOS)
body:
Use for customers who have lost all connectivity and see a red or blinking LOS light.

Procedure:
1. Check for a known area outage or planned maintenance on the network status dashboard.
2. Ask the customer to confirm the light pattern on the ONT (power, PON, LOS) and the fibre cable seating.
3. Run a remote line test and check whether the ONT is registered on the OLT.
4. If the ONT is offline with LOS, book a field technician visit within 24 hours.
5. Offer a temporary mobile hotspot data pack while the repair is pending.
6. Create an incident ticket and give the customer the reference number and ETA.

Escalation: if the problem persists after the steps above, raise a Tier-2 ticket referencing bb_no_internet and attach the diagnostics collected.

title: Duplicate payment / double charge refund process
body:
A customer was debited twice for the same invoice. Refund the duplicate to the original payment method.

Procedure:
1. Verify both transactions in the payment gateway and confirm they relate to the same invoice number.
2. Check whether one payment came from an autopay mandate and the other from a manual payment.
3. Raise a duplicate-payment refund request in the billing system with both transaction ids.
4. Inform the customer that refunds to the original payment method take 5-7 working days.
5. Disable the redundant payment method or autopay mandate if the customer agrees.
6. Send a written confirmation of the refund request reference.

Escalation: if the problem persists after the steps above, raise a Tier-2 ticket referencing bill_double_charge and attach the diagnostics collected.

title: Disputing unrecognised charges and value-added services
body:
Customers may contest add-on or proration charges. Always review the itemised bill first.

Procedure:
1. Open the itemised bill and identify the unfamiliar line items and their activation dates.
2. Check the order history for value-added service activations and the channel they came from.
3. Deactivate unwanted add-ons immediately and confirm the change with the customer.
4. If the activation was not customer-initiated, raise a bill adjustment for the disputed amounts.
5. Explain proration rules if the charge relates to a mid-cycle plan change.
6. Confirm the corrected bill will be reissued and note the adjustment id in the ticket.

Escalation: if the problem persists after the steps above, raise a Tier-2 ticket referencing bill_unexpected_charges and attach the diagnostics collected.

title: Autopay failure and late-fee waiver
body:
When recurring payments fail, resolve the mandate first, then consider a one-time late-fee waiver.

Procedure:
1. Check the autopay mandate status and the failure reason code in the payment gateway.
2. Ask the customer to re-register the mandate or update the card expiry.
3. Take a manual payment over the phone or the self-care app to avoid service suspension.
4. Waive the late fee once if the customer has a clean payment history.
5. Set a reminder to verify the next autopay cycle succeeded.

Escalation: if the problem persists after the steps above, raise a Tier-2 ticket referencing bill_autopay_failed and attach the diagnostics collected.

title: Poor indoor mobile coverage troubleshooting
body:
Weak indoor signal is usually a coverage or handset-settings issue. Work through the checks in order.

Procedure:
1. Check the coverage map and recent tower alarms for the customer's postcode.
2. Ask the customer to enable Wi-Fi calling/VoLTE and confirm the handset supports it.
3. Verify the handset has the latest carrier settings and the right network mode (auto 4G/5G).
4. Ask the customer to reseat the SIM and test it in another device to rule out hardware.
5. Log a coverage complaint with location details so Radio Planning can assess a small cell.
6. Offer a signal-booster/femtocell if the customer is eligible.

Escalation: if the problem persists after the steps above, raise a Tier-2 ticket referencing mob_no_signal_indoors and attach the diagnostics collected.

title: Frequent call drops
body:
Dropped calls can come from poor handover, handset or SIM issues. Collect timestamps for the radio team.

Procedure:
1. Check for network alarms and handover failures in the customer's usual area.
2. Ask the customer to toggle airplane mode, then re-select the network manually.
3. Reset network settings on the handset and re-test with VoLTE on and off.
4. Test the SIM in a second handset to isolate device versus network.
5. Raise a radio-quality ticket with timestamps of three failed calls.
6. Offer a SIM swap if the SIM is older than three years.

Escalation: if the problem persists after the steps above, raise a Tier-2 ticket referencing mob_calls_dropping and attach the diagnostics collected.

title: Slow mobile data troubleshooting
body:
Throttling and APN errors are the most common cause of slow data; check them before radio issues.

Procedure:
1. Verify the customer has not exhausted the fair-usage data limit and been throttled.
2. Check the APN settings and reset to the carrier defaults if they were changed.
3. Compare speed on 4G and 5G manually to detect a congested layer.
4. Check the cell congestion report for the serving site during the reported hours.
5. Raise a network optimisation ticket if the site load is above 80%.

Escalation: if the problem persists after the steps above, raise a Tier-2 ticket referencing mob_slow_data and attach the diagnostics collected.

title: Router rebooting or overheating
body:
Spontaneous restarts are usually power, heat or firmware related.

Procedure:
1. Ask the customer to check ventilation and move the router away from heat sources.
2. Check the router uptime and crash logs from the management platform.
3. Verify the power adapter model and replace it if it is not the original.
4. Push the latest stable firmware and factory-reset only if the issue persists.
5. Arrange a hardware replacement if it continues to restart after firmware update.

Escalation: if the problem persists after the steps above, raise a Tier-2 ticket referencing rtr_reboots and attach the diagnostics collected.

title: Wi-Fi coverage and dead zones
body:
Coverage problems are solved by channel selection, router placement and extenders.

Procedure:
1. Check the Wi-Fi channel utilisation and switch to the least congested channel.
2. Enable band steering or move devices to 5 GHz close to the router and 2.4 GHz at distance.
3. Advise placing the router centrally and elevated, away from metal and microwaves.
4. Offer a mesh extender or Wi-Fi pod if the home is larger than the router's coverage.
5. Verify firmware is current and transmit power is set to maximum.

Escalation: if the problem persists after the steps above, raise a Tier-2 ticket referencing rtr_weak_wifi and attach the diagnostics collected.

title: Recovering router admin access
body:
Factory reset restores admin access but removes custom Wi-Fi settings.

Procedure:
1. Verify the customer's identity before sharing or resetting any credentials.
2. Ask them to check the sticker on the router for the default admin login.
3. Guide them to hold the reset pin for 10 seconds to restore factory defaults.
4. Reconfigure the PPPoE/ONT settings remotely or via the self-care wizard afterwards.
5. Remind the customer to set a new strong admin password and Wi-Fi key.

Escalation: if the problem persists after the steps above, raise a Tier-2 ticket referencing rtr_admin_reset and attach the diagnostics collected.

title: New SIM activation failures
body:
Most activation delays are pending KYC verification or an unprovisioned SIM.

Procedure:
1. Confirm the SIM serial number is assigned to the customer in the activation system.
2. Check KYC / identity verification status and complete any pending verification.
3. Trigger a manual provisioning request and verify the HLR/HSS record.
4. Ask the customer to restart the phone and set automatic network selection.
5. Replace the SIM if the provisioning succeeds but the handset still reports invalid SIM.

Escalation: if the problem persists after the steps above, raise a Tier-2 ticket referencing sim_not_activating and attach the diagnostics collected.

title: SIM blocked / PUK unlock
body:
PUK is sensitive: only provide it after successful identity verification.

Procedure:
1. Verify the customer's identity with security questions before sharing the PUK.
2. Provide the PUK from the SIM management system and warn about the 10-attempt limit.
3. Guide the customer through entering the PUK and setting a new 4-digit PIN.
4. If the PUK is also locked, issue a free replacement SIM.
5. Suggest disabling the SIM PIN if the customer keeps forgetting it.

Escalation: if the problem persists after the steps above, raise a Tier-2 ticket referencing sim_puk_locked and attach the diagnostics collected.

title: Mobile number portability (port-in) delays
body:
Port-ins fail mostly due to expired UPC, name mismatch or outstanding dues at the donor operator.

Procedure:
1. Check the MNP request status and rejection code in the porting gateway.
2. Verify the unique porting code (UPC) is still valid and matches the number and name.
3. Resubmit with a fresh UPC if it has expired (valid for 4 days).
4. Confirm the customer has no outstanding dues with the donor operator.
5. Escalate to the porting desk if the request is pending beyond the regulated 3 working days.

Escalation: if the problem persists after the steps above, raise a Tier-2 ticket referencing sim_port_in_stuck and attach the diagnostics collected.

title: No service while roaming internationally
body:
Check that the roaming pack is active, then try manual network selection.

Procedure:
1. Confirm an international roaming pack is active on the account and not barred.
2. Ask the customer to enable data roaming and select a partner network manually.
3. Verify the destination country and partner operators are supported in the roaming agreement.
4. Refresh the HLR roaming location update remotely.
5. Advise the customer to restart the phone and, if still failing, switch to an alternate partner network.

Escalation: if the problem persists after the steps above, raise a Tier-2 ticket referencing roam_no_service and attach the diagnostics collected.

title: Disputed roaming charges
body:
If bill-shock alerts failed, a goodwill adjustment may apply.

Procedure:
1. Pull the roaming CDRs and confirm which sessions generated the charges.
2. Check whether a roaming pack was purchased and whether usage exceeded it.
3. Verify that the bill-shock alert SMS was sent at the threshold.
4. Apply the one-time goodwill adjustment policy if the alert was not delivered.
5. Recommend a roaming pack and data cap for future trips.

Escalation: if the problem persists after the steps above, raise a Tier-2 ticket referencing roam_bill_shock and attach the diagnostics collected.

title: Enabling international calling
body:
ISD is disabled by default on some plans or when credit limits are hit.

Procedure:
1. Check whether international dialling (ISD) is barred on the account.
2. Verify there are no credit-limit or unpaid-bill restrictions.
3. Enable ISD after identity verification and confirm propagation within 30 minutes.
4. Ask the customer to dial with the + prefix and country code to test.
5. Offer an international calling pack if the customer calls frequently.

Escalation: if the problem persists after the steps above, raise a Tier-2 ticket referencing roam_intl_calls_blocked and attach the diagnostics collected.

title: Plan upgrade and downgrade procedure
body:
Plan changes take effect at the next billing cycle unless an immediate change is requested.

Procedure:
1. Show the available upgrade plans and price differences for the customer's eligibility.
2. Explain proration and the effective date of the new plan.
3. Confirm any contract or lock-in impact before submitting.
4. Submit the plan-change order and give the customer the order reference.
5. Confirm the new benefits in the self-care app after 24 hours.

Escalation: if the problem persists after the steps above, raise a Tier-2 ticket referencing plan_upgrade and attach the diagnostics collected.

title: Relocating a connection / changing address
body:
Relocation requires a serviceability check before an order can be raised.

Procedure:
1. Check serviceability and fibre availability at the new address.
2. Verify the account holder's identity and capture the new address with a landmark.
3. Schedule a relocation appointment and agree the shifting fee (waived for contracts over 12 months).
4. Update the billing address effective the relocation date.
5. Send the confirmation with the technician slot to the customer.

Escalation: if the problem persists after the steps above, raise a Tier-2 ticket referencing plan_address_change and attach the diagnostics collected.

title: Cancellation and retention handling
body:
Always check contract status first and follow the retention playbook before disconnecting.

Procedure:
1. Check the contract end date and early-termination charges.
2. Offer a retention plan or loyalty discount appropriate to the customer's tenure.
3. If the customer insists, record the reason code and raise the disconnection order.
4. Generate the final bill and explain pending dues or refunds.
5. Confirm the disconnection date and equipment return instructions.

Escalation: if the problem persists after the steps above, raise a Tier-2 ticket referencing plan_cancel and attach the diagnostics collected.

title: Missing channels and entitlement refresh
body:
Missing channels are normally an entitlement-refresh issue; resend authorisation first.

Procedure:
1. Verify the customer's TV pack subscription and entitlement status in the middleware.
2. Send a refresh/re-authorisation signal to the set-top box.
3. Ask the customer to power-cycle the box and rescan channels.
4. If entitlements are correct but channels are missing, check for a channel-lineup change or outage.
5. Replace the set-top box if the smart card or STB fails authorisation after refresh.

Escalation: if the problem persists after the steps above, raise a Tier-2 ticket referencing tv_channels_missing and attach the diagnostics collected.

title: IPTV buffering and pixelation
body:
Buffering usually points to Wi-Fi or multicast problems rather than the content platform.

Procedure:
1. Check the customer's line stability and multicast/IGMP configuration on the router.
2. Ask the customer to connect the set-top box via Ethernet instead of Wi-Fi.
3. Verify QoS prioritisation for IPTV traffic is enabled on the gateway.
4. Reboot the set-top box and update its firmware.
5. Raise a media-quality ticket if multiple customers on the node report the same.

Escalation: if the problem persists after the steps above, raise a Tier-2 ticket referencing tv_buffering and attach the diagnostics collected.

title: Set-top box not booting / no signal
body:
First rule out cabling and broadband; then reset and re-provision the box.

Procedure:
1. Check that the HDMI cable and TV input source are correct.
2. Perform a hard power-cycle by unplugging the box for 60 seconds.
3. Verify the broadband line is up since IPTV depends on it.
4. Factory-reset the box remotely and re-provision it.
5. Book an engineer visit or replacement box if it still does not boot.

Escalation: if the problem persists after the steps above, raise a Tier-2 ticket referencing tv_stb_no_signal and attach the diagnostics collected.

title: Incoming calls not received
body:
Use when outgoing calls work but callers cannot reach the customer.

Procedure:
1. Check the line status and call-forwarding settings on the subscriber profile (unconditional and busy/no-answer).
2. Verify that Do-Not-Disturb or call barring is not active on the account.
3. Check whether the handset is registered on VoLTE and re-provision the VoLTE profile if it is not.
4. Ask the customer to toggle airplane mode and re-seat the SIM, then place a test call from another number.
5. Run a network registration trace (HLR/HSS) and escalate to core voice support if the subscriber is not attached.

Escalation: if the problem persists after the steps above, raise a Tier-2 ticket referencing voice_no_incoming and attach the diagnostics collected.

title: SMS and OTP messages not delivered
body:
Applies to missing text messages, especially one-time passwords from banks and apps.

Procedure:
1. Confirm the SMS centre number on the customer's profile is the operator default.
2. Check whether the number is registered on a DND/spam-filter list that blocks service messages.
3. Verify that the handset storage is not full and that the sender is not blocked on the device.
4. Send a test SMS from the support tool and check the delivery report.
5. Re-provision the messaging service on the SIM and escalate to the messaging gateway team if delivery reports fail.

Escalation: if the problem persists after the steps above, raise a Tier-2 ticket referencing sms_otp_missing and attach the diagnostics collected.

title: Voicemail setup and PIN reset
body:
Covers activation, PIN reset and mailbox problems on mobile voicemail.

Procedure:
1. Check that the voicemail service is active on the subscriber profile.
2. Reset the voicemail PIN to the default and tell the customer how to change it.
3. Ask the customer to dial the voicemail access number and record a new greeting.
4. Clear the mailbox remotely if it reports full after deleting messages.
5. Re-provision visual voicemail settings if the handset app still fails.

Escalation: if the problem persists after the steps above, raise a Tier-2 ticket referencing voicemail_setup and attach the diagnostics collected.

title: Spam, scam and phishing calls
body:
Use for unsolicited calls or messages; escalate immediately if the customer shared credentials.

Procedure:
1. Record the offending numbers and timestamps, and tag them in the fraud reporting tool.
2. Enable network-level spam filtering and register the customer on the do-not-disturb list.
3. Advise the customer never to share OTPs or PINs and to block the numbers on the handset.
4. Raise a case with the fraud desk if the customer shared credentials or money was lost.
5. Follow up after 7 days to check whether the volume of unwanted calls has dropped.

Escalation: if the problem persists after the steps above, raise a Tier-2 ticket referencing fraud_spam_calls and attach the diagnostics collected.

title: Suspected SIM swap or number takeover
body:
Treat as urgent: block the new SIM first, then investigate and add account protection.

Procedure:
1. Verify the customer identity with strong checks before discussing the account.
2. Check the SIM change history and the channel and agent that approved the latest swap.
3. Block the newly issued SIM immediately and restore service on the customer's original SIM or a fresh one.
4. Open a high-priority fraud case and tell the customer to contact their bank right away.
5. Add a SIM-change lock and extra verification to the account.

Escalation: if the problem persists after the steps above, raise a Tier-2 ticket referencing sim_swap_suspected and attach the diagnostics collected.

title: Unauthorised value-added subscriptions
body:
Remove the service, block third-party billing, and refund charges that lack valid consent.

Procedure:
1. List active value-added services and subscriptions on the line with activation dates.
2. Deactivate the unwanted subscription and block third-party premium billing on the number.
3. Check the consent record for the activation and mark it as disputed if there is none.
4. Refund the charges made after the unauthorised activation to the customer's balance.
5. Confirm in writing which services were removed and how to block future ones.

Escalation: if the problem persists after the steps above, raise a Tier-2 ticket referencing unauth_subscription and attach the diagnostics collected.

title: Missed or cancelled technician appointments
body:
Rebook promptly, confirm contact details and consider a goodwill credit for repeat misses.

Procedure:
1. Check the work order status and the reason code recorded for the missed visit.
2. Apologise and rebook the earliest available slot, prioritising the customer for the next day if possible.
3. Confirm the customer's contact number and access instructions before closing the booking.
4. Send an SMS with the new appointment window and the engineer's details.
5. Log a service-credit request if this is the second missed visit.

Escalation: if the problem persists after the steps above, raise a Tier-2 ticket referencing tech_no_show and attach the diagnostics collected.

title: Delayed new connection or installation
body:
Find the blocked order stage, give the customer a real date and escalate when the SLA is breached.

Procedure:
1. Look up the order and identify the blocking stage: survey, permit, cabling or provisioning.
2. Contact the field team for an updated completion date and note the reason for the delay.
3. Give the customer a realistic date and the order reference, and set a reminder to follow up.
4. Escalate to the provisioning manager if the delay exceeds the committed service level.
5. Offer a temporary mobile data solution or a credit while the installation is pending.

Escalation: if the problem persists after the steps above, raise a Tier-2 ticket referencing install_delay and attach the diagnostics collected.

title: Repeat faults after a technician visit
body:
Reopen the original incident, retest remotely and send a senior engineer with the visit history.

Procedure:
1. Review the notes and test results from the previous visit.
2. Run a fresh remote line test to confirm the fault is still present.
3. Reopen the original incident rather than creating a new one so the history is kept.
4. Book a senior engineer visit with the earlier findings attached.
5. Update the customer after the visit and close the ticket only after a successful 48-hour check.

Escalation: if the problem persists after the steps above, raise a Tier-2 ticket referencing visit_unresolved and attach the diagnostics collected.

title: eSIM transfer and activation errors
body:
Each eSIM QR code can be used once, so issue a new one after cancelling the old profile.

Procedure:
1. Verify the customer identity and confirm that the new device supports eSIM.
2. Cancel the old eSIM profile and generate a new activation QR code or code string.
3. Ask the customer to connect to Wi-Fi and scan the new QR code on the new handset.
4. Check that the profile status changes to active in the provisioning system.
5. Re-issue a new code if installation still fails, since each QR code works only once.

Escalation: if the problem persists after the steps above, raise a Tier-2 ticket referencing esim_transfer and attach the diagnostics collected.

title: Handset network unlock requests
body:
Unlock is available once the device is paid off and the lock-in period has passed.

Procedure:
1. Check that the device is fully paid off and the lock-in period has ended.
2. Verify the IMEI on the account matches the handset the customer wants unlocked.
3. Submit the unlock request in the device management system and note the reference.
4. Send the unlock code or confirmation to the customer, normally within 2 working days.
5. Explain the steps to enter the code on the handset and which SIM to insert.

Escalation: if the problem persists after the steps above, raise a Tier-2 ticket referencing device_unlock and attach the diagnostics collected.

title: Handset warranty, repair and replacement
body:
Confirm warranty coverage, rule out software causes, then raise a repair or replacement.

Procedure:
1. Check the purchase date, warranty status and whether the damage is covered.
2. Run the basic troubleshooting: restart, software update and factory reset after a backup.
3. Create a repair or replacement request and give the customer the service-centre address.
4. Offer a temporary handset if the repair will take more than 3 days.
5. Tell the customer the expected turnaround and the reference number to track the repair.

Escalation: if the problem persists after the steps above, raise a Tier-2 ticket referencing handset_repair and attach the diagnostics collected.
